items.headline: What OpenAI's latest controversy tells us about the future of math
items.excerpt: OpenAI says roughly 10,000 concurrent agents cracked a long-open problem in the Navier-Stokes family, but the claim is shadowed by accusations that it failed to credit the human mathematicians whose AI-assisted work it built on. The episode raises the question of whether frontier math now requires compute only a few labs can afford.

items.headline: Release of open AI model trained on 17 years of lunar data maps ice, craters and volcanoes
items.excerpt: NASA and IBM released an open-source lunar foundation model trained on nearly two decades of Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter data. It lets researchers identify ice deposits, impact craters and volcanic features with only minimal labeled training data.

items.headline: New AI model for DNA learns from evolution to unlock secrets of the human genome
items.excerpt: UC Berkeley's GPN-Star, a genomic language model trained on evolutionary signal, outperforms larger rivals at pinpointing the genetic variants behind inherited traits and disease. It does so while requiring far less compute to train than competing genomic foundation models.

items.headline: AI extracts interpretable constitutive laws directly from solid-mechanics data
items.excerpt: A graph-based framework from the Eastern Institute of Technology reads raw material-test data and writes out explicit, physically interpretable equations for how alloy steels, lithium metal and filled rubbers deform. It beat mainstream empirical models on predictive accuracy without becoming a black box.

items.headline: An AI tool aims to catch harder-to-detect heart attacks in EKGs
items.excerpt: The FDA granted a rare de novo clearance to Powerful Medical's 'Queen of Hearts' algorithm, which reads electrocardiograms to flag and triage heart attacks that standard criteria miss. It is one of the first AI tools authorized for occlusion-type infarcts invisible to conventional EKG rules.

items.headline: Lancaster University Leads Project on Quantum Neural Computing
items.excerpt: Lancaster University is leading IgnisQNC, a EUR 1.88M three-year European project fusing quantum computing with explainable AI. The goal is to turn quantum uncertainty into a computational resource for trustworthy machine learning rather than a source of noise.
